synonyms: Rubroshorea spp. (red meranti species, segregated from Shorea in 2022)
region: Southeast Asia: Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Borneo
description: Meranti, lauan and seraya are trade names for a large group of Southeast Asian Shorea (and related) species, grouped by colour into red, white and yellow meranti. The wood is used for joinery, window frames, doors, mouldings and especially plywood, where it is often sold as lauan or 'Philippine mahogany' even though it is not a true mahogany.

hazards.summary: The UK safety regulator lists skin irritation among the reported effects of meranti and lauan timbers.
Case reports describe hives on the skin after contact with meranti dust, and hives with runny nose and itchy eyes in a worker exposed to lauan (Philippine red mahogany).

Occupational asthma from meranti (reported as Shorea pauciflora, a red meranti) is listed in a peer-reviewed review of wood dust allergy; we have not yet confirmed the species in the original studies.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nasal cavity and sinuses after long-term exposure.

related_species_note: Trade names meranti, lauan and seraya cover dozens of species across Shorea, Rubroshorea, Parashorea and Pentacme, so a report about one may not apply to all. 'Philippine mahogany' is unrelated to genuine mahogany (Swietenia).

notes_internal: Genus-level entry. WFO (checked 2026-11-07) now treats Shorea pauciflora as a synonym of Rubroshorea pauciflora; many red meranti species moved to Rubroshorea, and some lauan species to Pentacme. Kept 'Shorea spp.' as the familiar name; a reviewer may prefer 'Shorea, Rubroshorea and related spp.'. Asthma rests on Schlunssen-2018 Table 1 (S. pauciflora, citing Vandenplas 1996 Thorax 51:472-478 and Kersten 1994). The Vandenplas abstract mentions wood dust only generically; species not confirmed, so it is not cited. Koh-2016 and Goransson-1980 have no PubMed abstracts; testing details not confirmed.
